speaker: The Chairman
text: Head X – Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Today, the global environment is more fractious and societies are increasingly polarised.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Disruptive technologies are changing our economies, our jobs, our way of life and challenging our norms.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Singapore is a global city state that is multi-racial, multi-cultural, multi-religious and in some way multinational is at the epicentre of these forces.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If we are not careful, these global forces can exert tensions that will threaten, disrupt and test the strength of the fabric of our society.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: While MCCY has done well in fostering a strong sense of national unity and pride through sectors of arts, youth, community and sports, new challenges such as the COVID-19, regional political turmoil and international trade tensions are always emerging and we must be prepared to remain resilient and stay united as one Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: MCCY must continue to strengthen the social fabric and the solidarity in the face of these forces.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Are the current MCCY's strategies still relevant in the building an inclusive home where everyone feels that we are equal members of the same community, and are given equal opportunities to thrive and to pursue one's passion and interest?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Given the increasing diversity and fractious state of our society, can we continue to progress together as a people?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: What unites us as one people, one nation?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Is it the Kallang Roar and Kallang Wave when Singapore Lions beat Pahang during the 1994 Malaysian cup?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Or the 50.39 secs that Joseph Schooling swam while we all held our breath in front of our TV screens during the 2016 Olympics?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Or the nail-biting table tennis finals during the 2008 Olympics when our paddlers brought us a silver medal?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We wept as a nation as we mourned together during the passing of our beloved founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew in 2015.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Today, we are again tested and challenged and tested with COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We are tackling these challenges together and collectively with resolute and resilience.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: As we continue to progress, the natural fault lines in our society – socio-economic divide, racial and religious divide, ideology divide, sexual orientation divide, e-literacy divide and many more – will continue to exist and may surface from time to time to threaten our resolve and unity.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Will we be able to rise to the occasion like previous challenges and emerge stronger or will we be divided and withered?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: MCCY needs to intensify the efforts in building a home that provides opportunities for all.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It is important while we embrace our diversity and differences as strength of our nation, we need to work hard to create and expand common spaces and experiences that is unique to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: One, use arts, culture and heritage unique to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Make of arts and cultural programmes more accessible and affordable to Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Two, renew and remake of community clubs to remain relevant so that more Singaporeans will visit and use the CCs.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Our CCs should be the Community Centre for arts, culture, wellness and health, social interactions and skills upgrading.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Three, expand and build up community sports that can unite and bring people together.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Chairman, building a home that provide opportunities for all is not just an ideal.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It is a basic right for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In Malay):   Our youths play a vital role in developing our community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MENDAKI has focused its efforts on providing educational support for youths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Some of MENDAKI's programmes include the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme and the Future Ready programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Emotional support is also important to prepare our youths for the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: How is MENDAKI supporting our youths in their emotional development?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singaporean Muslims live in a diverse multi-racial community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We face unique challenges that are different from Muslim majority countries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Asatizah play a crucial role in guiding our community to live a rich and confident social religious life in a multi-religious Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our asatizah have a profound impact on the outlook of Singaporean Muslims including how we practise Islam and how we interact with people of different faith.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Almost all our asatizah are trained overseas in Muslim majority countries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Could the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs provide an update on this programme?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: How else is MUIS preparing our asatizah to guide Singaporean Muslim community to live in a multi-cultural modern society?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   To effectively guide the Muslim community who live in a multi-cultural society, the community depends on the asatizah to dispense religious knowledge that is based on lived reality and are able to address emerging issues, such as cryptocurrency and plant-based food.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is important that the asatizah are equipped with the necessary skills to engage the community effectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: How can our asatizah further engage and contribute to the community’s needs, beyond that of a religious teacher?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Will MUIS provide assistance and support so that the asatizah are better equipped to contribute in the fields mentioned earlier?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Mohamed Irshad, take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, for the first cut, I wish to congratulate the Committee on Future Asatizah or COFA, led by Senior Minister of State Dr Maliki Osman, for completing its work.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: What can the asatizah fraternity expect from the recommendations?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The Singapore Muslim community is a highly diverse one that speaks a multitude of languages.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to a significant number of Indian Muslims who speak a myriad of languages, there is a growing resident community of Muslims who speak Tagalog, Mandarin and other north Asian languages.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We also have a large population of Muslim foreign workers who speak Bangla, Urdu and other South Asian languages.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Since 1998, when the first MUIS scholarship was awarded, we have groomed a generation of Malay asatizah who are highly educated and doing some amazing work on the ground.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: For my second cut, Chairman, the Greek philosopher Heraclitus' statement "Change is the only constant in life" is applicable to all of us and all our situations without exception.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: For our respected asatizah fraternity, this statement is especially important as they have donned the robes of responsibility of guiding fellow Muslims in their faith.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In order to be effective torchbearers and shepherds, our asatizah need to remain relevant by constantly updating themselves with knowledge, skill sets, contemporary issues, and even vocational skills.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I also note that the current generation of asatizah have the MUIS Academy which offers a range of courses and training as part of their lifelong learning ethos.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: There is also the SkillsFuture initiative for those asatizah who wish to acquire new skills.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In order to benefit from these effectively, our asatizah need to be more aware of the competencies they ought to possess.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: This will then enable them to make informed choices about improving themselves.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs share how MUIS will support the asatizah in this regard and the competencies they should acquire in order to stay relevant?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   Asatizah play an important role today in guiding the Singaporean Muslim community to help us thrive in a multi-religious and multi-cultural society, as well as globally, in addition to upholding our religious values.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: MUIS will also focus on efforts to enhance the professional development of our asatizah.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There are many ways for an ustaz or usatazah to contribute to society, but one of the common grouses amongst this group is that this sector appears to have limited employment opportunities.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What has MUIS done to ensure that the religious sector can become an attractive sector for employment, especially for the talented ones who can make good contributions?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It was also reported that a revision will be made to asatizah's wages.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What are the strategies that our community will support in order to ensure that our asatizah’s wages are aligned to market rates?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap, you take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This programme aims to provide holistic support to Muslim couples before and after marriage.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   I would like to get the following facts from the Minister.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: From this number of appeal cases that were reported, how many cases were reported by the ex-husband and how many by the ex-wife?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In fact, until today, I still receive similar feedback from time to time from some of my residents as well as the public.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, take your two cuts, please.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Preschool education plays an important role in the early years for better development and learning in the later stages of life.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In the last few years, there has been a growing emphasis on preschool education.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Early Childhood Development Agency has been pushing for more children to attend pre-school regularly so that they will not fall behind in their studies compared to their peers when they enter primary school.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is because the early years of childhood are important towards shaping social and communication skills as well as attitudes towards learning.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is a platform to give all children an equal start in life regardless of their backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   MENDAKI has been playing a crucial role in supporting career mobility among the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Last year, MENDAKI held its first Raikan Ilmu (Celebrate Knowledge) campaign, which celebrates the diverse bodies of knowledge in our society.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The campaign saw activities that encouraged both children and adults to explore knowledge in new areas such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and robotics.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I was very impressed by it and I hope to see further extensions of it soon.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Such campaigns are important and engaging reminders to the community to be open to learning new skills, especially in today’s economy where the rapid pace of growth has disrupted traditional industries and business models.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In Malay):   I had the opportunity to speak to several groups of asatizah at dialogue sessions organised by Berita Harian last year.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In the discussions with them, one of the issues raised was the challenges faced by the asatizah when they perform their duties to educate and provide guidance to the community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Among other things, the asatizah shared that our community members approach them to ask about new issues that they face, and therefore, the asatizah must have knowledge and a fresh approach to manage such issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The Malay/Muslim community needs to adapt religion within a new context that is different from the context long ago.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: From the way we connect in the cyber world, to the way we do business, to our medical treatments; much has changed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For example, MUIS has produced a compilation of fatwas (Islamic legal ruling) on issues related to science, medicine and health.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There have been many new scientific procedures and developments, and our community requires proper guidance.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: What is certain is that, with rapid global developments, there will always be new issues that our community must face.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Due to the ever changing needs of the community, our asatizah must also be equipped with the relevant knowledge to manage current issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Our young asatizah must have a very strong foundation in Islamic education as well as other relevant fields such as science and technology.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We must begin preparations as early as primary school.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We must develop a younger generation that is well-versed and comfortable with current issues so that they are able to handle future challenges.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They may also join other fields apart from Islamic education and therefore they should be prepared.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Chairman, as I previously mentioned in the House, the Singapore Muslim community is a highly diverse one.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: In addition to the racial diversity, we have Muslims from all around the world coming to study, work, marry and settle in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Like a garden of flowers, this diversity adds to the beauty and richness of the Singapore Muslim Community, in particular, the Singapore society at large.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: We have seen the introduction of Friday sermons being translated and at times being delivered in English and other languages.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   The 4G leadership recently expressed the Government’s strong commitment to partner Singaporeans of all races, cultures and religions, and working together with them in nation-building.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For the Malay/Muslim community especially, what are the new methods of engagement in which the Government is prepared to partner the Malay/Muslim community to co-create and collaborate in co-solutioning for issues faced by our community?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   In recent years, there have been many changes to the education system and landscape in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While we are part of the Malay diaspora in the region, there are three things that make our community unique – character, competence and citizenry, or what I call the 3Cs.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The first "C", character, is about the outlook of the community and the values that it cherishes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We cannot be successful if we are liabilities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The third and final "C" is citizenry, a sense of responsibility towards nation-building and society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We cannot be satisfied merely with being equal in rights, we must also be equal in substance as citizens.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Singapore is our home and we have a duty to it.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, in the midst of our fight against COVID-19, I want to start by talking about citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In a number of dialogues with the community, we received feedback that the community is happy with the support that the Government is extending to citizens in response to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am happier to see that the community is contributing where it can in the fight against the virus, not just happily receiving help.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, Masjid Assyakirin teamed up with Bo Tien Temple, representatives of the Baha'i faith, the Calvary Bible-Presbyterian Church and Jurong Christian Church to prepare lunch boxes and notes of appreciation for healthcare workers in Jurong Polyclinic.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In support of their initiative, Al Ayza Restaurant sponsored half the food and helped with delivery.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Other Muslim-owned restaurants, such as Kinamaya, Rumah Makan Minang, Hajjah Maimunah Restaurant and Positano Risto, also stepped up.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They teamed up with the riders of Dadah Itu Haram, who delivered the food to frontline healthcare workers in Singapore General Hospital.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mendaki, too, organised a walk to raise funds.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MESRA Youths made and distributed 1,000 ribbon flowers to our frontliners to tell them – we remember you.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many Malay/Muslims have been at the frontline in the healthcare sector, home team and even the passenger transport sector.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am proud they are standing shoulder-to-shoulder with fellow Singaporeans in this fight.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During this crisis, we see that citizenry is genuinely demonstrated.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Standing bravely at the frontline and stepping forward to help, exemplify character, the second "C" and one of the three qualities that our community wants to be known for.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As Muslims, character is closely intertwined with our religion, culture and therefore our identity.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There are many minority Muslim communities around the world that struggle with the practice of Islam in secular jurisdictions, multicultural societies and against contemporary challenges.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In Singapore, we are fortunate to have a strong fraternity of asatizah, who are also fellow Singaporeans and their guidance has made all the difference for our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: After extensive engagements, COFA found that the community would like to our asatizah to guide them on issues of the modern world and to see them connecting with other communities to build a cohesive society and contribute to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: My colleague, Senior Minister of State Maliki, will elaborate further on what we intend to do with COFA's recommendations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I agree with Senior Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin, who spoke about the importance of being able to address Muslims who live in our multicultural society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And as Mr Irshad said, there is diversity not just in our society, but also within our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We can look into grooming more religious leaders who can engage in various languages.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS will also work with our asatizah to develop a body of knowledge and practice to guide Muslim life in multicultural societies.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must also re-think the role of asatizah.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the past two years, the work of M3 has shown us that asatizah are well-placed to provide spiritual guidance and support in various facets of Muslim life, beyond the mosque and the madrasah.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They can provide pastoral care to the incarcerated, the sick and the aged.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They can be spiritual guides to couples, whether they are trying to build a new family or overcoming trials and tribulations to preserve the home.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked how the Syariah Court has handled the divorce cases that has come before it.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In my view, the more pertinent issue is to work with the community upstream in strengthening families and preventing divorces.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There are many ways an ustaz or ustazah can contribute.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Muslim community needs religious curriculum developers for our madrasahs, specialists to administer religious programmes in MUIS, ROMM and our mosques and jurists to support our Syariah Court and Fatwa Committee.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Importantly, we need asatizah who do not shy away from grappling with contemporary issues.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As a Muslim Singaporean, I feel proud that our asatizah have risen to the occasion.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, when NEWater was introduced, our asatizah sought to understand the water technology used and were quick to recognise that the end-product was clean and that means, also Halal.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Such clear-minded, progressive thinking is even more important in exceptional times, like now.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To minimise the risk of transmitting COVID-19, our asatizah gave guidance on bringing our own mats when we pray in the mosque and refraining from shaking hands for now.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Singapore is probably the only place in the world where Muslim religious leaders give practical, medically-sound advice with such speed.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: If we can train and enable more asatizah to support our community in these ways, our community will be better for it.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The job of an ustaz is not easy.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To perform his job well, an ustaz must not only be well-versed in Islamic knowledge, but also be au fait with psychology, sociology, social work, comparative law, science and technology and more.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As several of our Members of Parliaments pointed out, we must support our asatizah in this journey.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are therefore making an investment not only in asatizah training but also to transform the formal religious sector.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, how effective our asatizah are in nurturing the character of our community therefore hinges on their competence.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But for our community to succeed, we must also encourage every Muslim to aspire towards excellence and contribute to the community and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Inasmuch as the camaraderie amongst our healthcare workers and home-team members matters, it is also their competence that earned them the trust of Singaporeans in the fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As a community, we have come a long way.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We marshalled community resources to form MENDAKI, which then worked with MOE as a partner to develop a support system for Malay/Muslim students.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last year, our students outperformed their OECD peers in Mathematics and have made substantial improvements in reading.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As we move forward, we must try to make sure that all our students are able to acquire at least a Nitec – this is the "red-line" that MENDAKI must ensure no one falls below.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Concurrently, we must grow the numbers of our youth who can graduate with a University degree.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During my Hari Raya speech, I called this our "blue line" and MENDAKI must help as many as possible across it.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The truth is, addressing dropouts and failure rates are already problems of yesterday.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We need to prepare our young for a tomorrow that will be challenging and volatile.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In today's economy, ITE, Polytechnic and University qualifications are merely hygiene factors.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MENDAKI's efforts are only as good as it keeps pace with the changing educational, social and economic landscape.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Thus, we have started a comprehensive review of MENDAKI's policies and programmes, to ensure that MENDAKI can be an effective partner to MOE and our educational institutes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond that, there must be an equal emphasis on lifelong learning in our community, much like in the past, when we emphasised the importance of educating our children well.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We cannot just be focused on tax-rebate vouchers to manage today's cost of living.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our community must also take advantage of other forms of support like the SkillsFuture Credit, to acquire new competencies and qualifications for better-paying jobs, especially when their current skills run the risk of being irrelevant in the near future.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The same applies to Malay/Muslim SMEs and funding support for digitalisation and venturing overseas for them to grow.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Minister of State Zaqy will speak on the shifts MENDAKI will be making and how we are encouraging lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to conclude in Malay.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   Our community can do more to contribute in various areas and sectors.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many initiatives have been rolled out by our volunteers at M³@Towns with the close cooperation of MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In line with this measure, a series of conversations called CiptaSama@M³, was formed to hear the views of the Malay/Muslim community on national issues that are of greatest concern to them and to co-create solutions that can be implemented so that we can prosper together as a nation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have started the conversation with the leaders and volunteers of the M³@Towns and we look forward to engaging members of the community from all walks of lives in the coming months.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In building a Community of Success, we must continue to uphold the three key values of the community – Character, Competence and Citizenry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, our asatizah anchor our community to values and traditions in a rapidly evolving world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Increasingly, they are expected to dispense religious guidance on matters not limited to faith and rituals, but also on finance and estate matters, science, medicine and family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Demographic shifts, such as an ageing population, evolving concepts of gender roles and challenges brought forth with the Internet of Things, require clearer religious guidance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: COFA members included representatives from the asatizah fraternity, Malay/Muslim community leaders, professionals and academics from different fields.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These engagement platforms include focus group discussions, round tables, online surveys, street surveys and interviews.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: COFA concluded its deliberations with the following vision for future asatizah: (a) As religious leaders in a multi-cultural and diverse society, our asatizah must proactively engage on issues of the modern world and connect with other communities to build a cohesive Singapore society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (b) As professionals, our asatizah are advocates of lifelong learning, acquiring new knowledge and skills in guiding Singapore Muslims to respond to contemporary challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (c) As role models, our asatizah are rooted to Islamic traditions, resilient, adaptable, compassionate, driven and committed to the betterment of Singapore society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, a significant proportion of jobs in the religious sector are unstructured and, as Mr Zainal Sapari highlighted, this results in limited opportunities to progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This year, asatizah can look forward to the first initiative under AWDP, which is the Career and Competency Framework (CCF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This framework articulates the different roles and pathways within the formal religious sector and provides information on the respective skillsets needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With this framework, asatizah can better plan their careers and proactively learn about skills and competencies required for the various career pathways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the next three years, MUIS will develop more initiatives under the AWDP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This includes salary guidelines, a religious talent programme to identify and develop future religious leaders and more opportunities for skills upgrading.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The religious talent programme, like the Muis scholarship that Mr Irshad mentioned, will be open to deserving applicants on the basis of merit, regardless of race.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For asatizah who are interested to upgrade themselves on emerging issues, Muis will organise relevant courses on digitalisation and the use of social media.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Lifelong learning is crucial and critical for all Singaporeans who want to stay relevant, and our asatizah are no exception.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The top-up to their Skills Future Credit announced in Budget 2020 will be an additional boost for them to explore new frontiers of skills and opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As we nurture a stronger, more adaptable asatizah workforce, it is also important to strengthen religious institutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I agree with Mdm Rahayu Mahzam that madrasahs play an important role in developing future asatizah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS has been working closely with our madrasahs to support the development of teachers, improve programmes and curriculum and enhance the facilities of madrasahs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, Madrasah Al-Arabiah has a new campus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The campus is equipped with better lab facilities and resources for students, so that our young asatizah can build a strong foundation in both religious and secular subjects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) and Syariah Court also play key roles in the lives of Singaporean Muslims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While overseeing the registration and solemnisation of marriage and managing divorces will remain their core roles, these institutions can play a bigger part in shaping community life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The third strategic thrust is to nurture inspiring asatizah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: COFA saw potential for asatizah to contribute to adjacent sectors, such as social work, and to provide Singaporean Muslims with advice on how to navigate contemporary developments in the use of technology and finance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To help our asatizah step up to this role, the Postgraduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Societies (PCICS) will also expose them to social sciences, develop counselling, social work and other vocational skills to prepare them for an exciting and promising future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition to partnerships with renowned Islamic institutions like Al-Azhar University and the University of Jordan and our local publicly-funded Universities like NUS and SUSS, PCICS will include a practicum component to equip students with on-the-job training, exposure and experiential learning for their future roles in the workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay, please.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Our asatizah shape the character of our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In turn, I hope that our young aspiring asatizah will rise to the occasion, be the confident guides that the community needs to navigate future challenges and contribute to the vision of a Muslim community of success and help us build a strong and cohesive Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, let me touch on our efforts to strengthen our community’s competencies through MENDAKI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There are three drivers in today’s education landscape to provide the impetus for transforming MENDAKI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, good pre-school education is critical to the development of our children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Every child should have access to this, regardless of background.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Second, as Dr Intan Mokhtar has highlighted, our education approach in schools is changing and MOE is catering for greater flexibility in education for students with different abilities and interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Third, in a fast-changing world, lifelong learning is a must.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As Minister Masagos has mentioned, the community has shown significant progress in school dropout and failure rates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We can now focus on new challenges to take the community forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want our children to succeed in school and be equipped to achieve successful careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Dr Intan and Mr Saktiandi asked about our plans to support the pre-school sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For our young children, we want to equip them with a strong foundation so that they can achieve in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, if you put just $1 a day in your child’s CDA account, you will have $30 in a month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The money can then be used to pay for your child’s education and medical needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, contribute $1 and you get another $3 to support your child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: On the academic front, MENDAKI also started moving to pre-school last year with KelasMateMatika(KMM)@CC with the support of our M3 partners for Malay pre-schoolers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This programme reinforces basic numeracy skills and help parents to be more involved in their children’s development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year, more than 1,200 children and parents benefited from KMM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over 90% of parents who attended KMM said that they now recognise the importance of pre-school education and are confident on how to develop their children’s numeracy skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI is planning to scale up KMM to benefit more families this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The academic performance of our MTS students has been encouraging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In 2018, 60% of MTS students who took Standard Mathematics achieved at least one grade performance in their PSLE result, compared to their year-end result the previous year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, like Dr Intan said, we recognise the need to improve MTS, given our evolving education landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is why MENDAKI will review the MTS in five areas: (a) governance and leadership; (b) curriculum; (c) pedagogy; (d) professional development of our tutors; as well as (e) outreach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond educational support, I agree with Mr Amrin Amin that it is also important to provide emotional support and career guidance for our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With the support of other M3 agencies, MENDAKI has set up a Youth Mentoring Office (YMO) to grow a culture of mentoring in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We now have over 700 volunteer mentors and 200 of them are already on the ground to support our work with the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: A key aspect of the Budget this year was about supporting Singaporeans in lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The ability to upskill, adapt to industry shifts and be ready for new opportunities is key to staying relevant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Saktiandi asked how MENDAKI will be supporting the community in this area.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want to encourage our adults to take up various initiatives to support their learning, such as the SkillsFuture Credit top-up announced in Budget 2020.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is especially useful for our mature workers who are looking to improve their career prospects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI SENSE will continue to guide jobseekers and workers on how to make full use of these opportunities provided by the Government so that they can access desired jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our first Raikan Ilmu month reached out to about 30,000 participants and we hope to further our outreach to 40,000 this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to conclude in Malay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In Malay):   We are committed to providing end-to-end support, at every stage of life, for our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI is enhancing their initiatives in response to the changing education and employment landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This starts from efforts that encourage the learning and development of young children, to supporting the aspirations of youths, and building a culture of lifelong learning for adults.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In turn, we hope that the community recognises the importance of enhancing our educational standards and embracing the spirit of lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Come, let us double our efforts to become a highly competent community and continue to contribute to the success of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: (In Malay):   I would like to ask the Minister or Minister of State whether they can provide more information about the MUIS-MENDAKI Preschool Grant (MMPG).

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I welcome the support that will be given to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: More importantly, how can they apply for the grant?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Second, what will the Youth Mentoring Office (YMO), that Minister of State mentioned earlier, do for Malay/Muslim youths in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As for the second question – YMO was set up by MENDAKI, with the support of M3, to grow a strong culture of mentoring within our community.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Its objective is to provide career guidance which is a key aspect of this mentoring project.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It provides useful guidance for our youths especially those who want to pursue a career in new areas like AI, cybersecurity and others.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Although there are good career prospects in these areas, they may not know any role models who can help them to explore these pathways.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we hope that, with this Youth Mentoring Office programme, we can help them to find jobs and careers in new areas.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: (In Malay):   Minister or Minister of State Zaqy, what are the plans for MENDAKI's Tuition Scheme to ensure that our children are ready for a more dynamic environment and also to seize opportunities to excel in various areas apart from academic excellence?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will further strengthen the leadership and administration of these centres.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Second, we will also update the MTS curriculum and introduce the Science subject to Primary 3 students instead of Primary 4 currently.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Third, MENDAKI will also make pedagogical changes to further improve our children’s experience at the MTS.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For Primary 1 to 3 students, MENDAKI will explore various learning techniques, including experiential learning or modular learning outside the classroom.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Hence, learning should not only be conducted in the classroom but also outside the classroom.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For Secondary school students, MENDAKI will introduce Subject-Based Banding.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, we will be aligned with MOE by transforming the way we provide support, which will be tailored to our children's abilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To help students who require more guidance, MENDAKI will upgrade its intensive guidance programmes that it piloted last year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The results of this pilot programme has been encouraging so far.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MENDAKI will also look into the professional development of its 830 MTS tutors and also explore ways to empower parents so that they can be more involved in giving motivation and support to their children.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Lastly, MTS will further enhance its outreach strategy to engage students who need more support and this includes strengthening MENDAKI's involvement in schools with a percentage of Malay/Muslim students who are not performing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MENDAKI will collaborate with MOE in the UPLIFT programme so that more of our students who need academic support will receive a more comprehensive assistance.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: By 2021, MENDAKI hopes to work with 15 more schools so that we can increase the number of MTS centres to 100.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: (In Malay):   So far, there has been no cases of COVID-19 that came from the mosques in Singapore, even though many Muslims of different nationalities visit the mosque daily to perform congregational prayers.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Can the Minister share what steps have been taken by MUIS and the mosques to mitigate the risk of COVID-19 infection among mosque congregants so that everyone can pray safely and peacefully?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: (In Malay):   Thank you, Mr Zainal, for the question on COVID-19, especially in relation to our community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Obviously, when we congregate, for example, in mosques or during festivities, infections can occur.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the mosques, for instance, we will shake hands with each other.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the past, our ladies used the praying veils provided by the mosques.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Or our foreheads will touch the mosque’s carpeted floor during prayers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MUIS and the Mufti have given guidance so that we can momentarily change our normal practice.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For instance, please bring our own prayer mats to use during prayers because COVID-19 can be spread when someone coughs on the same carpeted floor that come into contact with our foreheads during prayers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If we want to shake hands, make sure that we have washed our hands first with soap, and after shaking hands, wash them again.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But I think if we are often seen washing our hands every time we shake hands, we will perhaps be seen as being disrespectful.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, my suggestion is to greet each other this way (Minister places his hand on his chest) while we deal with this COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But in time to come, as I said earlier, we must also further improve our level of hygiene, personally and for the individual, so that we take care of our health as well as our loved ones’ health.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is how we manage the COVID-19 issue for the long-term.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, I have three cuts, may I take them together?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Mr Chairman, our children are our country's future.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The environment that our children are living in and growing up with is very different from ours, as will be case from generation to generation.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: But the world today is economically more uncertain and is more polarised and fragmented with opposing camps holding deep, uncompromising views.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Disruptions, dis-intermediation and shifting of economic powers globally have threatened the existing world order and has triggered the competition for hegemony among global nations.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Our children and youth have a stake in Singapore's future as influencers for change.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: As the Government, we must ensure that we provide opportunities for our children and youth to grow and develop holistically.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: How is MCCY supporting equal opportunities and holistic development for our children and youths?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Arts and sports, for instance, are crucial ways to nurture the young.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: And studies have shown that participation in arts and sports can bring about positive cognitive, behavioural and social outcomes.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: How will MCCY ensure that all children and youth, regardless of their background and ability, have access to arts and sports opportunities?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: As our youths enter the workforce, we must also ensure that they are equipped with the skills and knowledge to thrive, especially when the future of work has yet to be defined.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: How can MCCY work with the other relevant Ministries to ensure that we prepare our youth adequately for future workforce challenges?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Mr Chairman, culture is a way of life.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: It is the social glue that binds different communities together.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: It creates shared beliefs among people and a common identity that helps define the character of the nation.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: And in many ways, the Botanic Gardens and our hawker food are part of our cultural and national identity.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: We grew up with hawker food and everyone has our own favourite hawker stalls and, of course, we would always remember strolling through the Botanic Gardens with our loved ones.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Some of us here in the House might even remember strolling through the Botanic Gardens and then going to the hawker centre across the road for some excellent murtabak, dessert and drinks.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Yet, culture is not only defined by UNESCO titles, neither can culture be created by attaching labels to empty physical spaces.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Culture exists only when people attach special meaning and importance to places or to practices, and only when places and practices hold personal memories to people.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: So, the places where we live, work and play hold many memories about our traditions and way of life, which make us uniquely Singapore.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's cultural heritage belongs to us all.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The different communities living and working in Singapore are all part of our cultural fabric and the different communities need to define for themselves what is culturally important to them, while also celebrating the aspects of other communities.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: As the Government, we need to empower our community stakeholders to celebrate their heritage, promote their heritage in everyday spaces, and more importantly, facilitate its transmission to the next generation.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Can MCCY share how it intends to continue to engage the community to sustain interest in, and deepen appreciation for Singapore's cultural heritage?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: With less than five months to go before the Tokyo Olympics, can MCCY provide an update on how Team Singapore athletes, especially the up and coming ones, are faring regionally and internationally?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Mr Chairman, the uncertainties surrounding COVID-19 and the high rates of infection in Japan have also thrown a bit of a spanner in the works.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: There is the possibility of COVID-19 being declared as a global pandemic and there is thus the possibility of the Tokyo Olympics being significantly affected by this as well.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: How is MCCY supporting Team Singapore's preparation in the lead up to the Tokyo Olympics and Paralympics?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: And how does MCCY plan to support Team Singapore athletes if they were to compete in a host-country where the rate of COVID-19 infection is high?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: With the kick-off in May 2019, can the Ministry provide a progress update on the discussions so far?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What are the aspirations and ideas from our youth, resulting from this engagement and what can youths look forward to in 2020 and beyond?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The transformation of the Somerset Belt designated as an area with a strong youth focus as part of the longer term plans for Orchard Road is also a key project under the SG Youth Action Plan.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What has been the progress of discussions and how will the slowdown in the economy impact its development?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: It is gratifying to note that in the recent years, more Singaporeans, particularly youths, have been coming together to form ground-up initiatives ranging from upcycling to urban farming to evolving traditional arts and so on.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Will MCCY continue to support these ground-up initiatives through Our Singapore Fund?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Besides enabling ground-up initiatives, how is MCCY supporting the Government’s efforts to partner Singaporeans in shaping our future Singapore together?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Volunteers play an important role alongside social service professionals to shore up the social safety networks and reduce the number of cases of people falling through the cracks.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: But, of course, volunteer work can be a lot more than helping the needy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Volunteers are also needed to run community gardens, do befriending, look out for the interests of the environment and wildlife, and so on.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: In short, they are crucial towards building up the resilience of a nation through encouraging cohesion and compassion.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: During COVID-19, we saw how volunteers are playing crucial roles in facilitating mask distribution efforts, including that in Toa Payoh, and ensuring attendees of community events partake in hygiene measures as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on these Volunteer Centres, and whether there are plans to roll out more Centres to more towns?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Henry Kwek, take your two cuts, please.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore’s caring and kindness, along with progress in our society’s civic, culture, and sports arena, are fuelled by the passion of our country’s volunteers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: MCCY has done an excellent job to identify, nurture, and empower them.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: We need to look no further than Team Nile, our Museum Volunteers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: MCCY also rolled out an excellent cloud-base volunteer portal, Volunteer.sg, that is a game-changer on how VWOs engage volunteers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I am deeply appreciative that MCCY has included Kebun Baru as a pilot within PA.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Last year, MCCY rolled out Volunteer Centres in seven towns to grow and coordinate volunteer supply, facilitate partnerships between community partners and build capabilities in these towns.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on these Volunteer Centres, and whether there are plans to roll out the Centres to more towns?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Most arts and culture institutions rely on a combination of ticket sales, grants, donations and endowment income.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: For those with NAC grants, the Government usually ties the grants to public attendances and projects that benefit Singapore, and rightfully so.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In view of the current circumstances regarding COVID-19, donations from some parts of the business community may be down and there can be reduced demand for large scale public performances.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Some institutions without deep reserves or large endowment could face significant challenges.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Can MCCY share how MCCY and NAC can better support these institutions in this difficult times?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: For example, can NAC provide additional support or convert existing grant by getting these institutions to invest in capability development, so that they can emerge stronger from the crisis?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: And three, removing the cap on the amount or percentage of budget that can be spent on paying project owners, since they are often the ones putting in the most time and effort into the project, and for manpower needs to be assessed on a case-by-case basis?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, since 2009, the annual Pink Dot SG has attracted tens of thousands of Singaporeans to attend in support of the LGBTQ+ community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: However, many Singaporeans have also expressed concerns about Pink Dot SG and some have organised counter-events such as Wear White.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Unfortunately, divisions along this fault line may nonetheless deepen, given the role other social divides, such as religion and age, play in shaping attitudes towards LGBTQ+ issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles or IRCCs have served an important role in strengthening social cohesion through dialogues, workshops and other programmes, amongst various religious and racial groups.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Yip Pin Xiu, you can take the three cuts together.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I declare my interest as a current athlete.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: It was formed after the Vision 2030 exercise to redefine the role of sport in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: One of the four Strategic Themes in Vision 2030 is ‘Sport without Boundaries’ where sports should be inclusive, with opportunities for people of all abilities to participate.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: DSMP was born to address gaps in the existing ecosystem to provide support for disability sports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: For the past three years, DSMP has been able to react and address some of these gaps.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I am highly appreciative of the planning and investment.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps it is timely that we now do a stocktake, and review what had worked, and what are new opportunities that may not have been available when DSMP was first implemented.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: So far, the DSMP team has come up with three disability sports programs which is the Play-Ability, Yes!

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I Can and Intro a Sport, There are plans to make sports complex more accessible.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Para Sports Coaching courses have been organised and there has been outreach and engagements, opportunities for volunteers.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: From an initiative started out to fill gaps, we should now look at the whole landscape and think of how to build bridges of opportunities with other sectors that work closely with PWDs, to maximise the potentials of the DSMP, with strategic execution.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I firmly believe that this plan has the ability to determine the speed of success for Sports Without Boundaries in Singapore in the long run.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Is a second version of the DSMP in the works, to review the landscape, and build bridges of opportunities, and support more aspects of disability sports?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: While programmes and infrastructure are improving, we should also leverage existing investments to promote access and build affinity for inclusion.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: My peers and I have gone through the exact same experience during our school days.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I have been told to sit out and look after school bags while the rest of my classmates were in PE class.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We were looked at differently, as if PE was something that did not matter to us, yet somehow essential for able-body students to gain different benefits, like teamwork and social networking.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Schools can be supported to convert existing CCAs to welcome suitable students with disabilities, while specialised CCAs on para sports can provide a setting for students with and without disabilities to increase interaction and develop inclusive partnerships.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If the children of today are exposed to this I believe that there is a higher chance they will grow up thinking that being inclusive is normal.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The students will learn that it is possible to adapt, to include the people around them. and people with disabilities are not that different from them.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The landscape will change not only for our youth with disabilities but will also lay a strong foundation in our young for a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: As a model, the DSMP should also encourage inclusive partnerships at a higher order, such as having Special Education Schools included in the School Sports Council.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Third, in a study highlighted by the DSMP, most VWOs, now called social service agencies, overlook the benefits that sports and physical activity can bring to PWDs and their overall well-being, due to the sources of their funding.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: It confused me that sports were not considered to contribute to psycho-socio well-being, where in fact an annex in the DSMP was dedicated to this.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Are we able to review programmes and capability funding to social service agencies to promote sports, and reduce “oversight” of such benefits?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Fourth, with transportation being highlighted as a critical factor preventing sports participation, can we explore expanding the current transport subsidy schemes and assistive technology schemes to support PWD in pursuing Quality of Life activities, such as sports?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: While most employers are benefiting from grant schemes to redesign jobs and work environments to employ PWDs, soft skills are equally important to PWDs for employability.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: However, if one of the aim is to build awareness and strengthen affinity with Team Singapore athletes, is there a possibility for DSMP to look at the entire spectrum of disability sports, from outreach to development to performance, and work with the current existing stakeholders in the respective areas to maximise efficiency of the resources?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In the last COS I raised the topic on Integrating National Sports Systems.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: To date, while there have been national sport systems that have voiced their interest in inclusion, concrete steps are still missing to support this progression in a systemic manner.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We can have a challenge fund under Sport Singapore to encourage NSAs towards integration.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The Disability Sports Master Plan plays a big role in increasing participation and making Singapore a more accessible, inclusive and caring community.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I am very eager to be a part of this ecosystem while we move towards our vision of Sports without Boundaries.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The next phase of the DSMP can help to build bridges with various ministries and partner social service agencies to enable Singaporeans where they can have a better quality of life and lead an active and healthy life through sports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: As an athlete, I have seen many of my peers face pressures from their sport, academics, work, and different aspects from their life.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: These pressures can sometimes affect their mental well-being.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Athletes retiring and transitioning out of sports can also find it difficult mentally and emotionally as most athletes have been doing this sport their whole life and it is their identity.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, the support for sports psychology is excellent.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: However, the support is for athletes to perform at a highest level and they may not be trained to help athletes with their mental well-being or any mental health issues.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The One Team Singapore Fund serves as a multiplier to help sporting organisations level up their high performance.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Most National Sports Associations (NSAs) are small outfits and work very hard to source for funding.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: One way is to market the NSA or its athletes to secure sponsorships, where it then becomes a win-win situation for both the NSA and the sponsor.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: We look forward to hearing from the FAS on their plan to achieving their stated goal and how the football fraternity, community and the Government can support them in their efforts." Sir, I have been looking forward and waited since September 2019 for updates from the Football Association of Singapore or MCCY.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: This time around I do hope to hear some positive sharing from the Minister on the matter.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Coincidentally, true sporting nations typically display such positive attributes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, I recall that the Committee of Sporting Singapore report in 2001, championed by Mr Goh Chok Tong, articulated these three desired outcomes of a Sporting Singapore, the other two being "vibrant society and economy" and "international friendship".

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Minister Grace Fu was quoted by Straits Times on 16 January 2020 that: "There’s so much more that we can do before we can really call ourselves a sporting country”.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But we have made progress, and I cite the example raised by Senior Minister of State Sim Ann in Parliament on 5 November 2019 that more people with disabilities (PWD) are participating in sport, with the Government exploring how a related master plan can make more progress.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Rewinding back the clock: in 2010, Singapore was awarded: the Gold for Sports City Award at the 2010 International Sports Events Management Awards, and Runners-up for the 2010 Ultimate Sports City at the Sports Accord Convention.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The international sporting community took notice of this little red dot’s sporting achievements during the 2001 to 2010 period.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The job creation objective was catalysed by the startup of Singapore Sports School in 2004, the launch of UK Loughborough University’s sports science degree in partnership with NTU, the emphasis of sports health leisure by Republic Polytechnic, ITE, and other private institutions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Working under MOU partnerships, the EDB, the previous Media Development Authority and Singapore Sports Council successfully courted international companies to relocate to Singapore and thereby created new jobs, for example, ASICS, Decathlon.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For this national iconic project, much has been said about the Public Private Partnership model; however, the sporting fraternity has yet to see positive changes that will convince Singaporeans that we have the right private sector partner running this national project.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: From public reports, there has also been critical changes to the shareholders and key partners: for example, the 83% majority shareholder Infra Red Capital Partners has been acquired by Sun Life.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Will it further impact negatively the desired outcomes of the project.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Are we getting value for money for this national project.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On this subject, I would like to appeal to MCCY once again.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Tampines has Our Tampines Hub; Bedok has Heartbeat @ Bedok; Sembawang has Sembawang Integrated Hub.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: A rundown swimming complex opened in 1988 and an old sports stadium opened in 1992.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The remaking of our sports facilities is to remain relevant and affordable, and to meet demands of the community.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure that the population of Yishun town has grown, and Yishunites deserve more and better sporting facilities.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Terence Ho, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Amid the evolving of the COVID-19 outbreak, the arts community brings people together, spreads love and positivity.
