speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In my previous speeches, I mentioned that I believe that a more targeted and well-defined Culture Matching Fund (CMF) policy can help small, medium arts groups in Singapore enjoy the benefits.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: To battle the economy downturn, I propose to review and reconsider the CMF.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This is a period for all arts groups; with the sudden cancellations and postponement of shows, arts groups are predicted to experience a deficit within the period.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: More help is definitely needed to bring back audiences and assure them that the shows will go on.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The COVID-19 outbreak has an impact on the worldwide economy and it takes time for the outbreak to settle down.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that there is a need to path a recovery route for all arts groups and is vital and to make the arts vibrant and accessible to the public again.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   During this trying period, operations of arts groups have been seriously affected.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The sustainability of arts and cultural groups require strong Government support, and also sponsorship and donations from corporates, foundations and individuals who recognise the importance of arts and culture.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In my previous speeches, I suggested that the Government exercises greater flexibility and adopt a more targeted approach in the administration of the Cultural Matching Fund (CMF).

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For example, aside from providing matching grants according to the amount of funds raised, the Government could perhaps consider providing matching grants according to performances and ticket sales.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This will help to increase funding for cultural and arts groups, who can then use the funds to tide over this period.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Bringing back audiences to performances cannot be done overnight.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: However, I believe that if arts groups unite together and go all-out to attract audiences, the crowd will come back, and the entire arts scene will be rejuvenated.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: How to canvas for donations and sponsorships beyond Government funding is the greatest challenge faced by most arts groups.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We hope to nurture more fans of the arts, including those who appreciate the arts and those who are willing to sponsor arts activities.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This is the hope of many arts groups.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: I also hope that arts groups can attract new audiences, who will eventually become advocates for the arts, and that all arts performances will enjoy such good ticket sales that only standing room will be left.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Arts groups now and in the future will require a significant amount of space to express their creativity and store their props and sets.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The arts space will help artistes and arts groups to grow and we need to keep up the growth of the arts group.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: With limited land space in Singapore, it is increasingly difficult to increase the gross floor area (GFA) of the arts community.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Do we have a short, mid and long-term plan to cater to the growing needs and create space synergy for the arts?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Earlier on in September 2019, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng announced that arts freelancers will have an arts resource website, and will also have dedicated working spaces.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In my previous speeches, I proposed that the Government can consider a central shared warehouse for the arts community, where props and sets can be stored, shared or reused.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This is one of the ways we can do our part to save the Earth from climate change, reducing wastage and disposal issues.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to that, perhaps the Government can consider including shopping malls and even unused national monument space, to cater for arts use.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, Wild Rice is housed within Funan and Singapore Dance Theatre is housed within Bugis+.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: We can integrate arts and culture within malls, to further increase the audiences’ reach.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Furthermore, as the world continues to face challenges during this outbreak, the local arts community is doing their part to rally Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: For example, the Theatre arts groups came together, to promote and share about each other’s’ upcoming productions.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: To battle the virus together, I propose the following.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This will help to tide the arts groups through this difficult period of low attendance and cancellation of their shows.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Two, can there be introduction of shared services among the arts groups, in terms of Professional Services such as legal advice, audit and accounting services?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: This can help reduce the expenditure of the arts groups.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: The synergy of arts space can integrate, interest and ignite the collaboration among arts groups and utilise resources to the fullest.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Amidst the challenging periods again, I am certain that the local arts community will continue to do their part to rally Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: My wish is that the dance will continue, the music will not stop playing, and we can live life as per normal.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They also provide opportunities for learning, communication and entertainment.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Therefore, it is important to ensure that culture and the arts are accessible to individuals from all walks of life.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Every segment of our society, including the less privileged, should have access to a wide range of quality arts performances.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In Singapore, free, non-ticketed arts events are widespread and easily accessible.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Last December, the Singapore Chinese Orchestra gave a free performance in an open area at my market/hawker centre.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My residents, especially the seniors, were delighted to have a wonderful concert at their doorstep.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They spent a memorable evening singing along with the evergreen hits and nostalgic tunes.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It was a most heartwarming sight and I really want to thank our hon Nominated Member Mr Terence Ho and Singapore Chinese Orchestra (SCO) for making this happen.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our seniors are really looking forward to the next one, which is coming up soon.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Quality arts performances can be expensive to produce and affordability would be an obstacle for the less privileged.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They may require interlocutors to provide context to the performances and may need to attend such events with friends and family to feel comfortable and to enjoy the performance.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, I would like to echo Ms Joan Pereira's call for arts to be accessible to all, regardless of socio-economic status.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Besides looking at the issue from the perspective of consumers of arts and culture, is MCCY also looking at the issue from the perspective of the providers of arts and culture?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Do our artists have the physical space as well as the platform to practice as well as showcase their craft.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is important to ensure that we have a diverse and vibrant arts scene.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are there plans to rejuvenate Gillman Barracks and also open up other locations for our local artists?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Apart from pursuing economic goals, we should also have room for the intangibles of life: to understand our history, appreciate our heritage, celebrate our diversity and participate in artistic expressions of various forms.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Thanks to years of consistent investments, we can be proud of having world-class venues in performing theatre, museum and art gallery.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Singaporeans have ready access to world-class concerts, performances and exhibitions.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Arts and culture, however, should not be confined to the premises of museums and concert halls.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Instead, they should flourish in the daily lives of our people.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Visitors to Italian cities such as Florence would see amazing sculptures and magnificent architecture at piazzas, along streets and on their buildings.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: In my constituency, we work hard to bring arts and culture into the community.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Our choir, orchestra and interests groups put up pubic performances.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: We are grateful to PA, NHB and NAC for their support and partnership.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: When Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong opened the Heartbeat@Bedok on 4 February 2018, we unveiled a locally-installed art work named “Pulses”.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: Singapore is no Florence but we could still envision our version of renaissance.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: Given this context, would the Minister enlighten us how MCCY views arts and culture development in the community?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan
text: Would MCCY support more ground-up initiatives on visual arts including installation of art works at public places, with programme akin to URA's "The Art Incentive Scheme"?

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Twenty-twenty marks the beginning of a new decade.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For MCCY, we ended the last decade on a strong note across our domains, where Singaporeans came together to celebrate our heritage, our unity and our sporting achievements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We commemorated our Bicentennial, recalling our history and how together we built a nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our religious leaders came together to affirm their Commitment to Safeguard Religious Harmony at the inaugural International Conference on Cohesive Societies.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have become a more caring nation through voluntary acts of spontaneous and everyday kindness.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There have been many accounts of how Singaporeans have looked out for each other in recent weeks during the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Many of us desire to do more for the community, from donating to volunteering.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As a people, we have become more confident about our identity, what we can offer and showcase to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We look forward to the outcome in December 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Making Singapore our home together is the heart of MCCY's work.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We believe in collectively shaping the society we want to be – a caring people, a cohesive society and a confident nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We work closely with partners to support the Singapore Cares movement.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We encourage our citizens to step forward to serve, through Team Nila and Youth Corps Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have expanded opportunities for Singaporeans to engage in honest dialogue and understand each other better, through programmes such as BRIDGE.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We partnered stakeholders to support the expression of national pride through Our SG Arts Plan and Our SG Heritage Plan.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We empower our citizens through Our Singapore Fund, Our Harmony Fund and the National Youth Fund, to start ground-up projects that can inspire others and strengthen our identity as one people.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With the Singapore Together movement, MCCY will do more to partner Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In a world where people are increasingly tribal, divided and disconnected from each other, we will ensure Singapore’s social fabric remains strong, by working together to offer opportunities, community and inclusion to every member of society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will enhance access to opportunities, foster a more caring and gracious community, and build an inclusive city of possibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For a society to be united, it must work for everyone, not just a few.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There must be equal conditions for all to thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I am glad Dr Lim Wee Kiak raised this.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will enhance access to opportunities in the sports, arts and youth sectors for all Singaporeans at each stage of their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Darryl David asked how MCCY will provide such opportunities for all children and youths.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In the early pre-school years, a child's main way of learning and developing is through play.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Under our Children and Youth Sport Framework, we will provide more in- and out-of-school play opportunities for our children to support their physical and intellectual growth.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2017, SportSG initiated the Nurture Kids programme to complement ECDA's development framework for our young children.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will also partner MOE to ensure all pre-school teachers graduating from the National Institute of Early Childhood have the skills to help our children develop their fundamental motor skills.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Complementing these initiatives, an "Active Parents" movement will be launched this year, to encourage and equip parents to play an active role in our children’s sporting journey.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: At our Primary and Secondary schools, we will continue partnering MOE to provide our students with opportunities for a well-rounded education through sports and culture.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2020, we will expand the School Sports Partnership and introduce "Active Play".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Primary schools can tie up with SportSG to conduct different sports, so students can pick up these sports conveniently – during recess, school sports days or at nearby sports centres.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These non-competitive arenas can encourage students to try more sports and bring them enjoyment while fostering confidence, teamwork and cohesion.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are also exploring more offerings under the Strategic Partnership CCA pilot formed last year between MOE, the National Arts Council (NAC) and SportSG.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This allows students to pursue their interests, even if these are not offered as CCAs in their schools.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They will be able to represent their schools in national competitions and platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Athletics and Ethnic Dance are currently offered under this programme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This year, where there is demand, SportSG is ready to open up more locations to support Athletics training.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On its part, NAC will work with LASALLE College of the Arts to provide Ethnic Dance experiences for interested students.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will nurture creativity and expand horizons of our children by celebrating our history and igniting their love for our heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For instance, there will be a permanent exhibition on "Singapore, Our Home", where children can learn how early pioneers lived and worked, and role-play as hawkers, coolies and merchants.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The museum will re-open in 2021 and add to the current offerings for children, such as the Children’s Biennale at National Gallery Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our museums will also provide our students with shared experiences of learning together and appreciating Singapore's history.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Students will travel through the museums in small groups, interact with museum educators and complete hands-on activities with their friends.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For instance, at the National Museum, students can learn the struggles of the Japanese occupation by choosing artefacts they are interested in and having conversations around those artefacts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: One such artefact is Elizabeth Choy's dress, which she wore while held captive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through this experience of exploring our history as a cohort, we hope our students will form shared memories together, and learn important values such as self-determination and helping one another during difficult times.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These initiatives will make learning more meaningful and come alive for students, as they go through their Character and Citizenship Education syllabus and subjects such as Social Studies in Primary school and History in Secondary school.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In an age where Asia's economy is growing in significance, our youths need to understand regional markets to thrive in the future economy.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) already provide youths with opportunities to build their economic, social and cultural awareness of the region.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Youth Corps Singapore piloted the enhanced Youth Expedition Projects (YEP+) in 2018 to provide youths with deeper understanding of the region.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The YEP+ comprises not only of community service, but also visits to multinational corporations and start-ups.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our participants have made their marks in Indonesia, Laos, Vietnam and China.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Currently, the YEP+ provides about 5,000 opportunities for regional exposure.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2020, we will increase opportunities for youths to engage the region.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The AEP will curate industry-focused experiences in the region for our youths to be more aware of the economic opportunities in these countries.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is double the current number of youths benefiting from NYC's programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will contribute to the "70-and-70" target for students, announced by the Finance Minister in his Budget Speech and enhance the Asia-readiness of our future workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Not forgetting those who are less youthful, we will ensure everyone has opportunities to lead full and active lives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be at or above the age of 65, and we will have 900,000 seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Sports and physical activity allow our seniors to sustain their health and mobility longer and continue to be engaged in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will review the age criterion from time to time, in keeping with the trends and life expectancy of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: SportSG will also partner the Agency for Integrated Care to bring programmes for seniors to their doorsteps, at Senior Citizens' Corners and Senior Activity Centres.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I have touched on new initiatives for Singaporeans at each stage of life.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Equally important, we must ensure that access to the things that make a full life – the beauty of the arts, the rigour of sports, the knowledge of our heritage, the support of our community – is open to all, regardless of background.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will continue to increase access to sports facilities around the island, under our Sports Facilities Master Plan.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This year, we will break ground for the new Punggol Regional Sport Centre.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will bring new Sport-in-Precinct facilities to Sengkang South, Pasir Ris East and Dover, achieving our target of initiating 20 Sport-in-Precinct projects by 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will rejuvenate another five ActiveSG facilities, from swimming complexes in Ang Mo Kio, to, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah may like to know, sport centres in Yishun.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In partnership with MOE, over 90% of suitable Government Primary and Secondary schools' sports halls and fields have been converted for public use under the Dual Use Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will work with MOE to convert all remaining suitable facilities by this time next year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These initiatives will help realise our aspiration of having sports and recreational facilities within a 10-minute walk from our homes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked about broadening access to the arts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Mr Terence Ho made similar suggestions in this House.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will ensure that all Singaporeans have access to quality arts productions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As Mr Terence Ho noted, everyone has a part to play in enhancing access to the arts and we encourage volunteers to step up and work with Social Service Agencies to see how they too can contribute their time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to speak in Malay.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: (In Malay):   We will enhance access to opportunities for all.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For our preschool children, we will help train the teachers to stimulate their physical and intellectual growth through.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For our school-going children, we will provide a more holistic learning journey, by expanding avenues for them to try new sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will also provide more opportunities in building shared experiences through learning our national history together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For post-secondary youths, we will increase opportunities for them to gain cultural literacy and a deeper understanding of the region.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will ensure our seniors can lead full and active lives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will ensure that everyone has convenient access to sports facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will also ensure that our lower income families will be able to enjoy quality arts productions, so we can all flourish as a society together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: However, such opportunities alone do not make a good home.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We must enable and help one another to succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Every Singaporean counts, we will only by progressing together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As a people, we need to recognise and act on our mutual obligations to our fellow citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: (In English): Beyond providing opportunities for all, we wish to build a strong community spirit where we care and help one another.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There is more each of us can do to give and to lift the less fortunate and more vulnerable among us.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Senior Minister of State will provide more details on these initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will deepen our commitment to one another as one people and to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2020, MCCY will partner Singapore citizens to create content on what makes us Singaporean and this content will be used to update our Singapore Citizenship Journey.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through this process, Singaporeans will articulate and affirm who we are as a people, while co-creating content to enrich new citizens' understanding of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: After an open call in January, we will convene a Citizens Workgroup comprising of interested persons from diverse fields and organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Over the next few months, they will discuss what unites us as Singaporeans and research topics close to our hearts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This would include our values and obligations as Singaporeans, social norms and our culture and national history.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: When we affirm our common fate, support one another and work and progress together side by side, we live a democracy of deeds.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Senior Minister of State will share more on this.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Ms Anthea Ong and Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked how we will support ground up efforts better.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Government will co-invest the balance in partners across all domains to support projects that address shared priorities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This enhanced support will help partners develop capacity and capabilities to sustain impactful initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: More immediately, Senior Parliamentary Secretary will also speak on our measures to support the arts and sports communities in view of the ongoing COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To grow an inclusive society that embraces diversity, we will expand pathways to success that celebrate our diverse talents, skills and cultures.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This year, we will provide more support to our athletes and artists, so they can excel and succeed and make Singapore a place of opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will support promising athletes representing Singapore who are not covered by our High Performance Sports system.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will work with individuals and groups to preserve our heritage in innovative ways and keep it alive so we can transmit it to future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Even as we celebrate what makes us different, we need to emphasise and protect what we share in common.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A major reason for Singapore's success is that we stay open to the world while remaining cohesive as a nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We combine unity with diversity, harmony with difference.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We can do this because our communities hold our differences not in opposition to each other, but in a relationship of mutual respect.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Diversity ensures we have the range and breadth of ideas, perspectives and resources to thrive globally.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Because we come from different lands and cultures, the possibilities of what we can make together are so much richer.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We see a common good and are committed to building something better.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We rely on one another for security, stability and prosperity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked how we will foster mutual understanding on LGBTQ.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In many of our discussions with citizens, the issue of sexual orientation has often been raised.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through such platforms, we listen to those different from us and seek to understand them on their terms, even with our disagreements; we expand the common space to engage one another and work together on the things that we want in common.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: When we drop the mindset of "us versus them" and see ourselves as a collective "we", Singaporeans with different points of view can sit together and work on issues important to our shared future, such as jobs and economy, the environment, the vulnerable and the disadvantaged.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will continue to support partners and agencies to build capacity and capabilities within the community for more inclusive civil discourse.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will support platforms that bring together people who hold different perspectives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And we will partner ground-up efforts to promote social harmony.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: (In Mandarin):   Apart from the recent COVID-19 situation, racism, religionism, and protectionism are also on the rise globally.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: People are increasingly tribal, divided and disconnected from each other.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As such, we will ensure Singapore's social fabric stays strong, by working together to offer opportunities, community and inclusion to every member of society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Bearing in mind our vision, we will build a home that provides opportunities for all, by enhancing access to these opportunities and allowing people to develop their full potentials.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will also foster a more caring and gracious community, where we do not forget to help and enable one another to succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will build an inclusive city that celebrates our diverse talents and cultures.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: (In English): To conclude, Sir, we in MCCY often ask ourselves if we are making progress towards our vision of a caring people, cohesive society and confident nation for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are aware that the strength of our society is not measured by, say, the number of art events we hold, or the amount of grants made.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The answer lies in our responses when we face a major crisis as a nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: COVID-19 is the moment that allows us to search for the answer.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To get through the crisis, we must unite around our values of multi-racialism, openness and self-determination.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We must not let fear and anxiety come between us.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: That it is a worldwide crisis gives us a good basis of comparison with others.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore has united as one, and acted and applied our minds to help one another.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Many have stepped up to show what it means to be Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Those working at the frontline of our defence are standing tall and stoically in their positions despite shouldering risks to themselves and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Some contributed time and resources to those in need, going deep into the community to reach out to seniors and the vulnerable in their homes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As the situation developed, more of us have come forward to help, in whatever way we can to anyone, regardless of race, language or religion.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is a testament to the strength of our society and our progress as one people.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And I think years of developing that support on the ground whether it is through PA, whether it is through Team Nila, our Youth Corp Singapore, have shown us we have the strength, a very strong and firm layer of volunteers that is out there that will support us, the Government, in reaching out to the ground and helping the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And I think this is the day we have been practising so hard, that we are preparing so hard for.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And I think Singapore has really come well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And through our actions, we demonstrate that we are in this together, with trust and confidence in the Government and in one another.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Together, we are working out solutions to new problems.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is the Singapore Spirit and the heart of our nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore Together is our commitment to partner Singaporeans to build a "democracy of deeds", as Deputy Prime Minister Heng shared last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The past weeks have shown how much we have grown as a democracy of deeds, with many rising to the occasion and having contributed to the common good amidst our ongoing fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last month, Team Singapore bowlers packed and distributed masks and hand sanitisers to seniors in Clementi.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Lim Sio Yen and Mr Ernest Koh Jun Ming set up video booths at various malls inviting people to record messages of support for those working in sectors such as healthcare, transport and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We believe that many who have made the first step of giving will continue to do so, inspiring others along the way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over time, our society will grow as a community of open hearts and helping hands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This matters because no one – not the Government, the private sector, or people sector – has a monopoly on good ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We can only find the best solutions to build a better future we all share, through partnership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In 2019, youths such as Greta Thunberg, made global headlines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In Hong Kong, Chile, Lebanon, Sudan, young people were at the forefront of civic protests and calls for change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Policy-makers and thinkers pondered how youths are different and what that means for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In Singapore and at MCCY, we began the process of engaging youths in 2018, with the Youth Conversations, a safe space for youths to talk about their aspirations and concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Like their elders, youths care deeply about their families and have the drive to succeed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are also topics where they have a different outlook.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If we do not listen to or work closely with our youths, these differences will lead to miscommunication, frustration, and divergence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Youths are also keen to move from conversation to action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These insights spurred us to refine our engagement approach to emphasise scale and more tangible impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we supported youths in envisioning and actualising their ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Yam asked for a progress update on the SG Youth Action Plan, and what youths can look forward to this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is our most ambitious youth engagement exercise yet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: A diverse panel of youth leaders compiled thousands of youth voices into a draft vision of what youths hope to see in our near future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And here is what it says: "Before we change the world, we must first change ourselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We may not always get it right, but with hard work, compassion and determination, we will foster an inclusive, sustainable and progressive Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will create a home where Singaporeans care for one another, and have a fair shot at their dreams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Twenty-twenty five, we are coming for you!" The draft youth vision conveys youth priorities, and provides us with a positive sense of what Singapore’s future will look like when the youths of today become the movers and shakers of tomorrow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We invite youths to help us refine this vision further.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have already begun empowering youths with information, resources, and networks to turn their ideas into reality.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the purpose of the Youth Action Challenge or YAC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The inaugural YAC saw 250 youth participants in 57 teams consult industry experts and policymakers to prototype ideas on the themes of environment, society and jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I witnessed some of these teams’ pitches in January, and was impressed by their passion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Allow me to share two examples: Team Movement of Inclusivity is keen to help frontline staff in public spaces better assist persons with hidden disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another team, Team ASEAN Business Youth Association, wants our youths to become more ASEAN-savvy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, they built a prototype platform offering regional networking opportunities for youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There will also be further editions of the YAC for youths to drive change on new themes that they care about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The SG Youth Action Plan will also focus on championing youth concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Panel partnered the Youth Alliance on Mental Health to call for more whole-of-society action in reducing stigma, strengthening peer support, and tackling workplace discrimination.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The recently announced Youth Mental Well-being Network will build on the work of the SG Youth Action Plan to co-create solutions with our youths and different segments of society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I am excited by the progress made and I look forward to more areas in which our youths will make a difference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The second aspect of our new approach is to create more opportunities for youths to re-shape Singapore’s spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Youths have helped to co-create the Somerset Belt Masterplan, which Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey will share more about later this month, including how youths can enliven the Belt through their own initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Youths can also look forward to co-creating and co-owning the youth hub within Kallang Alive!, a sporting and lifestyle destination from our sports blueprint, Vision 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our youths are energetic, and have an edgier take on sports and the arts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The youth hub will be a space for such dynamism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Details of engagements with youths will be shared later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The third way we are approaching youth engagement differently is through NYC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NYC will be a conduit for youth voices by expanding its digital engagement channels so more diverse segments of youths can provide candid feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It will also build its capabilities to support public agencies in identifying emerging youth needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also experimenting with ways for youth leaders to directly engage agencies on specific policy issues where they have relevant expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NYC will also be an incubator of youth action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Youths will receive greater support, through NYC’s curated leadership development and business exposure opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   The year 2019 was shaken by the youth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Youth made global headlines, as they were at the forefront of protests and calls for change in cities around the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Is this an indication that the next generation is better than the previous one, or, are they causing trouble for the world?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This led many policy makers and thinkers to ponder how youths are different from their elders and what that means for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Here in Singapore, we began that process in 2018 with the Youth Conversations, where we provide youth a safe space to share with us their aspirations and diverse viewpoints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Youth Conversations showed us that there are areas where youths bring to the table a different outlook.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We should work together with them to cultivate this as a strength and move from conversation to action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That is why we embarked on a new approach of engaging our youths for greater scale and a tangible impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To support youth to realise the vision, we started the Youth Action Challenge which empowers them with the information, resources and networks to co-create projects on issues they care about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to expand opportunities for youth to take actions and be heard in sustained manner, so that they can play an active part in building our home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Volunteerism is an important means of realising our youths' vision of a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Everyone has a part to play, not just youths, but seniors, corporates and Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, YCS launched Programme X – X standing for multiplier – to equip youths to start impactful community projects and lead their peers in turn.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over 400 youths from ITEs, Polytechnics and Universities have taken part in Programme X.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Sky Tai, a student from ITE College West, was one of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Following the programme, he designed and ran eight weekly arts sessions for seniors at SASCO Home in Hong San together with his teammates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Programme X enabled him to hone his leadership capabilities and deepened his resolve to serve the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: YCS is also working with our SG Cares Volunteer Centres to promote youth volunteerism and grow youth volunteer networks in the neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Seniors also wish to remain socially active and engaged in their retirement years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To reach out to more pre-retirees at their workplaces, we signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with RSVP Singapore last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: A new Team Nila Silver Champions Scheme will also provide seniors with regular volunteering opportunities at Active SG Sports Centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This includes training alongside Team Nila youths to serve as ActiveSG ambassadors to promote sport and exercise together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Seniors will also receive training through SportSG and WSQ courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On the corporate volunteerism front, NVPC and ComChest formed a closer partnership last year to help corporates access resources more easily and find better matches to volunteering opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over 30 corporates have been referred to our SG Cares Volunteer Centres to link up with community organisations for volunteering opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Henry Kwek asked for an update on our SG Cares Volunteer Centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our aim is to establish an SG Cares Volunteer Centre in each town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As "community brokers", our SG Cares Volunteer Centres form partnerships with organisations, such as schools, to channel their volunteers to community organisations in a mutually beneficial way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They also assist community partners with volunteer management, through efforts such as holding joint volunteer training sessions for community partners that may not have the capacity or the know-how to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have been working closely with several SSAs, such as Loving Heart Multi-Service Centre and Filos Community Services to helm our SG Cares Volunteer Centres in Jurong East and Bedok respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the past two years, these SSAs forged over a hundred partnerships with corporates, schools and other SSAs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We commend their hard work and invite more community-based organisations to partner us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Care is also manifested by ensuring that spaces are inclusive and providing opportunities for all to enjoy pursuits such as sports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Yip asked about updates to our Disability Sports Master Plan (DSMP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: She shared suggestions to expand play opportunities for persons with disabilities (PWDs) and build partnerships to promote inclusivity in sport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to work with community partners on inclusive programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are expanding events, such as Play Inclusive, an inclusive sports competition, to offer more opportunities for persons of different abilities and special needs to train and compete in sports together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also supporting Goalball Singapore to bring sighted and low-vision students to play sports together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SportSG also offers guidance to staff of SSAs to introduce inclusive sport activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are developing two frameworks to guide Special Education schools and SSAs on cultivating a lifelong enjoyment of physical activities for their students and clients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The adaptive swim framework focuses on teaching basic swimming and water safety competencies and the Fitness 1-2-3 framework focuses on imparting strength and conditioning knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The DSMP also provides opportunities to participate in High Performance Sports, as Ms Yip suggested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Individuals with potential from ActiveSG and community sports programmes are referred to the Singapore Disability Sport Council and the National Disability Sports Associations for further development and training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Singapore Sport Institute (SSI) also provides facilities, funding and specialist support for para athletes preparing for major games.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will follow up with her on her ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also want to support our charities and encourage giving through this time when we are all fighting COVID-19 as one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This year, we are also introducing sector-specific digital solutions for smaller charities to operate more efficiently and more securely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These solutions aim to reduce administrative burdens, improve productivity and provide higher protection against cyber threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Charities will also receive a digitalisation toolkit to expand their digital knowledge and capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also simplifying the process of searching for charities' information on our charity portal to help donors make informed giving choices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Each charity's profile page, starting with those that are IPCs, will feature information about how well the IPC is governed, for example, its level of regulatory compliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will be engaging charities and the public on what information should be shared, and how it can be presented in a useful way later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The giving culture is strong in Singapore, and we want to sustain it and grow it further by encouraging those interested to give through a new national legacy giving initiative, developed in partnership with CFS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Legacy giving refers to a planned, future gift that designates a portion of a person's assets as a donation to charity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Examples of such assets include cash and insurance policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our goal is to foster a giving mindset, where planned gifts to charity become more common and more frequent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is not just about bestowing financial assets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Legacy giving also imparts values such as kindness, compassion and generosity, which are far more lasting than assets alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Acts of care and contribution go a long way, especially in these challenging times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, MCCY will continue to pursue partnerships to uplift those in need and nurture an active citizenry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together, we can build a democracy of deeds as our legacy to future generations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, the arts, heritage and sports play an important role in making Singapore a vibrant and liveable city.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They bring people together, inspire them and root us as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Earlier, Minister and Senior Minister of State spoke about our efforts to build a home that provides opportunities for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is exemplified through the celebration of different pathways to success for our artists and athletes and the nurturing of a vibrant arts and culture ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The partnership among the Government, arts patrons and arts community forms the basis of a sustainable arts scene.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Terence Ho asked how MCCY will support the arts community during COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We want cultural performances to continue during this time as the arts inspire us and lift our spirits, as long as necessary precautions are in place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is what MCCY agencies and institutions, including NAC, NHB and PA will commit to, where possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We also want to encourage arts and culture practitioners to take this opportunity to develop their capabilities and better position themselves for the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, NAC will provide a one-time, enhanced capability development grant for individuals and arts organisations, to promote upskilling and organisational capability development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These two initiatives are part of the Support and Stabilisation Package announced by Deputy Prime Minister in Budget 2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Arts groups and practitioners, including those who already enjoy subsidised rentals under NAC's arts housing scheme, can benefit from both these initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The package also the new self-employed persons' (SEPs) training support scheme recently unveiled by MOM.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Under this, all SEPs will be paid an hourly $7.50 training allowance when attending eligible programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will continue working with SkillsFuture Singapore on a curated list of arts and culture courses for arts freelancers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will complement existing initiatives, like the Arts Resource Hub, which is working with partners to provide shared services in areas like legal and financial matters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We encourage all eligible arts and culture professionals to tap on the available measures, including subscribing to the Arts Resource Hub, which is free, and prepare themselves for the post-COVID-19 upturn.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Mr Ho suggested, we encourage arts practitioners to support one another during this time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SportSG is also engaging stakeholders, especially coaches and fitness instructors to use this time to retool and upskill through various courses offered by CoachSG and partner institutions, supported by SkillsFuture Singapore and SkillsFuture Credits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Sports coaches registered with the National Registry of Coaches (NROC) can apply for financial assistance under the Coach Development Grant to attend courses and programmes to upgrade themselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MOM's SEP training support scheme will also benefit these sports freelancers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will also ensure that our arts spaces are effectively used.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked for an update on the Gillman Barracks Art Cluster.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Gillman Barracks provides Singaporeans and tourists access to high quality arts programmes through educational art and history tours, performances, as well as talks and workshops by long-term tenant galleries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This includes the current edition of the Singapore Biennale, which had tours led by seniors and concerts by students from Ngee Ann Polytechnic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Two successful editions of SEA Focus in 2019 and 2020 also enhanced Gillman Barracks' standing as a locus of Southeast Asian Art.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Terence Ho asked if we will provide more shared spaces and resources to bring people together via arts activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To facilitate networking and to optimise available spaces, arts practitioners will have access to our arts centres.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In January, we opened two physical spaces under the Arts Resource Hub at Goodman Arts Centre and Stamford Arts Centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Plans are underway to have a third physical hub at Waterloo Street by early 2021 that will offer incubation and presentation spaces for arts freelancers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These plans complement schemes like the Community and Sports Facilities Scheme to provide artists with greater access to spaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I encourage more arts groups to consider how they can pool their resources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Those with existing facilities, for instance, could share them with others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, technology will also be used to strengthen our arts eco-system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC is collaborating with NLB to develop a National Online Repository of Singapore Arts to facilitate access to information on Singapore arts and deepen the expertise of arts researchers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will complement other digital platforms, such as the Cultural Concierge and Offstage, which seek to widen the public's engagement with the arts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Sports also plays a crucial role in strengthening our community bonds.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about our plans for a sporting Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As part of Vision 2030, SportSG is partnering stakeholders to develop a strong sporting culture and grow our standing as a major sporting hub through local and international events, such as the Singapore Rugby 7s, FINA World Cup and the Standard Chartered Singapore Marathon.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This figure excludes growth areas like sports broadcast, infrastructure projects, sports events and conferences, as well as e-sports, which SportSG, Enterprise Singapore and Singapore Tourism Board and local and international businesses have been seen working together to develop the e-sports scene.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The precinct has seen increased footfall, with regular activities such as quarterly Community Play Days and a variety of programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Like many Singaporeans, we want to see it succeed as the integrated sports and lifestyle destination that we envisioned.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have made our views and expectations known and SHPL agrees that Sports Hub should be a place that all Singaporeans can be proud of.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SportSG is in regular communication with their top management and closely monitors performance to ensure that agreed standards for availability of facilities and performance are met.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, SHPL is required to meet a minimum number of sporting event days at the National Stadium and Singapore Indoor Stadium each year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Where they have not met the standards, they have been held accountable and financial penalties have been imposed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to monitor and hold SHPL accountable to meet all their contractual obligations to deliver a first class and vibrant sports entertainment and lifestyle hub for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Darryl David asked how our athletes have fared internationally, how we are supporting our younger elite athletes and athletes who are competing in locations with a high rate of COVID-19 infections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On the international stage, shuttler Loh Kean Yew beat two-time Olympics champion Lin Dan to win the Thailand Masters last year, and he defeated the world number two shuttler at the Badminton Asia Team Championships in February.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Bowler Cherie Tan made history by becoming the first Singaporean to be named the World Bowling Athlete of the Year by World Bowling last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In para sports, swimmer Yip Pin Xiu clinched two medals at the 2019 World Para Swimming Championships while archer Nur Syahidah Alim became the first Singaporean to be named Para Women World Archery Athlete of the Year for 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Looking ahead, we now have more than 10 athletes across six sports who have qualified for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics; and nine para-athletes who have qualified for the Paralympics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These athletes are supported through the spexScholarship programme or dedicated campaign funding for the games, as well as annual Government funding through the National Sports Associations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Specialised sport science and sport medicine support is also provided to help them achieve their best.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For athletes going overseas, SportSG, together with the Singapore National Olympic Council and the Singapore National Paralympic Council, have developed detailed contingency plans to ensure the safety of our athletes and officials.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The contingency plans for Tokyo 2020 are being developed and will include measures and precautions for athletes and officials with regard to COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will also enhance our sporting infrastructure to support our youth athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
