text: The National Youth Sports Institute (NYSI) satellite facility will move to a bigger facility at the former Police Coast Guard Headquarters, next to the Kallang Basin in April.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will allow NYSI to scale up sport science support for more youth athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The new premises will be close to Singapore Sports Institute (SSI) and the Sports Hub where many athletes train, thus providing opportunities for interaction between the junior and senior athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Yip Pin Xiu shared that she has seen many athletes face mental pressures from their sport and their daily lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To ensure the mental well-being of athletes, the SSI sports psychology team has been equipping our athletes with skills to adjust to life post-competition and a post-sport career.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They offer counselling services and a mental health literacy programme, Mind Matters, that helps athletes and coaches identify and understand mental well-being issues as well as when and how to seek help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We note Ms Yip Pin Xiu's comment on the programme's limited reach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SSI is working to expand the reach of this programme to benefit more athletes as well as partners under the spexBusiness network to offer professional development support and opportunities for retiring athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our athletes can also look out for one another.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I encourage our retired athletes and veterans to take the lead to build circles of support, lend a listening ear, offer advice and help one another.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap asked about our plans for the Singapore national football team qualifying for World Cup 2034.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Government does not interfere with the management of our National Sports Associations, including the Football Association of Singapore (FAS).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We were briefed by FAS on the plans for Goal 2034 and have given FAS feedback.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We look forward to hearing back from them on their plans and how we can best support them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Supporting our athletes and artists is a shared endeavour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have funds to encourage private and corporate philanthropy for the arts and sports, reinforcing the Singapore Together movement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Terence Ho and Ms Yip Pin Xiu asked about the Cultural Matching Fund (CMF) and One Team Singapore Fund (OTSF) respectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We recognise that smaller arts groups may need more help as they lack strong fundraising capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will help these groups with the new Sustain The ARTs Fund, or stART Fund for short.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This fund will bring together donations from corporations and individuals, which will be matched by CMF where eligible, to support small arts groups in developing robust governance structures and attaining charity and eventually Institutions of a Public Character (IPC) status as well as programming.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: All eligible donations will receive prevailing tax deductions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In the sports arena, the One Team Singapore Fund (OTSF) complements the Government's investment in the high performance sports system by allowing individuals and corporates to make cash donations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We wish to clarify that similar to other Government matching funds, the OTSF does not provide matching for commercial arrangements like sponsorships as the fund aims to encourage philanthropy to sport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: More details will be announced in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, I have spoken about how we are supporting our artists and athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We agree with Mr Lee Yi Shyan that arts and culture should be accessible to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since 2012, we have established 21 arts and culture nodes across the island to provide quality arts programmes in our neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through programmes such as PAssion Arts, Arts in Your Neighbourhood and Artseen, we have co-designed community arts programming with the community and other partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have also brought arts and culture outside the confines of concert halls and museums and into public spaces during events such as the Istana open house.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through NAC's Silver Arts Programme, we have arts programmes designed for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To provide youths with opportunities to showcase their creative talent and energy, NAC has partnered *SCAPE to roll out the BUSKING@*SCAPE programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Under this programme, Singaporeans between 15 to 35 years old are not required to go through auditions or be endorsed under NAC's Busking Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Instead, they can register for time slots to busk at the prominent *SCAPE front-of-house which faces Orchard Cineleisure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The scheme was piloted from October last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To date, more than 60 young buskers have showcased their talents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To provide buskers with greater access to spaces, NAC will gradually introduce the concept of busking zones at Singapore River and Ang Mo Kio from April this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Each zone comprises a cluster of busking locations, allowing buskers the flexibility to move between them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This offers a more varied busking experience for audiences and ensures equitable access to popular busking spots.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will continue to engage venue partners and the busking community to review busking locations, manage busking activities and co-develop suitable programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I hope my fellow members will also offer your constituencies for buskers to perform.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will also develop a digital scheduling tool for buskers to pre-book their performance slots.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With this, members of the public and venue partners can look forward to more vibrant spaces and a diverse busking calendar.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Darryl David asked about community engagement efforts to safeguard our cultural heritage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will do this in partnership with the community, through public education and outreach, research and documentation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This year, there are two highlights – the Stewards of Singapore's Intangible Cultural Heritage Award and the outcome of the UNESCO Hawker Culture in Singapore nomination in December.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The safeguarding, promotion and transmission of our intangible cultural heritage (ICH) will not be possible without the contributions of our ICH practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These individuals will be honoured at the inaugural Stewards of Singapore's Intangible Cultural Heritage Award ceremony held in conjunction with Singapore Heritage Festival this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the past year, we were heartened by the strong support from the community for our UNESCO Hawker Culture in Singapore nomination.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to strengthen community support through platforms such as the Singapore Heritage Festival, community events and travelling exhibitions to schools to celebrate our hawker culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are lucky to have hawkers who continue to work tirelessly to serve Singaporeans amid this COVID-19 period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NHB museums, heritage institutions and community galleries will partner local shop owners to create "mini museums" within their shops to showcase their history and heritage, trades and products through information panels, displays of historical documents, photographs and artefacts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Street Corner Heritage Galleries may also develop programmes, such as tours and workshops, and participate in events such as Singapore Heritage Festival and the respective Culture Festivals of the heritage institutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Loong Fatt Tau Sar Piah along Balestier Road will host one such gallery.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With a history dating back to 1948, visitors to the family-run business can watch the stallholders mould the dough, stuff with mung bean filling and bake using traditional gas-fired ovens.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have prepared some tau sar piah for tea later.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These places will serve as reminders of our living heritage and anchor our memories as we move into the future together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, I will continue in Mandarin, please.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):   Singapore's rich history and diverse heritage belongs to every Singaporean.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To sustain a culturally vibrant Singapore, it is important that we safeguard and promote our nation's rich and diverse intangible cultural heritage, as this defines our identity as Singaporeans and it is a duty we must fulfil.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Beyond our shared stories and knowledge, our heritage is also embodied in our neighbourhood icons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In order to bring our heritage to neighbourhoods where we live and play, museums, heritage institutions and community galleries operated by NHB will partner local shop owners to co-create Street Corner Heritage Galleries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These local shops will function as "mini museums" to showcase their history and heritage, trades and products through displays of historical documents, photographs and artefacts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We hope to encourage people to appreciate the heritage embodied in their daily lives through the lens of our heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While our efforts to preserve and promote our intangible cultural heritage are ongoing, we have also diligently planned for the future by working on the succession of our heritage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There are risks threatening our local cultural heritage, traditional skills and craft, such as a lack of awareness or lack of interest in learning and passing them down.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the past year, we have been heartened to see strong support from the community for our UNESCO Hawker Culture in Singapore nomination.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In the coming year, we will continue to build community support through different platforms to celebrate our Hawker Culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to safeguard and promote our intangible cultural heritage through different channels and plans, ensuring that more Singaporeans may come to understand and appreciate it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, at MCCY, we are committed to providing opportunities for all, growing a democracy of deeds and nurturing a vibrant home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our work covers a wide range of areas – arts, heritage, youth, sports, community relations and the strengthening of a giving culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: At its heart, our efforts seek to make Singapore a caring, cohesive and confident nation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There is much we can achieve by working hand-in-hand and by encouraging individuals and groups to come together for the common good.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Let us continue to celebrate our collective achievements and build a shared future together.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah

text: Yes, the clarification is that there is a lack of event in the Sports Hub calendar that attribute to the high rental cost and high variable cost, according to the industry feedback.

text: Is it to generate and encourage mass participation at the grassroots level?

text: If so, then why is ActiveSG stepping into the arena of elite sports?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Example of this include football where ActiveSG is running elite programmes and also in tennis, where ActiveSG is running at elite academy with Voyager from Australia.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: These programmes undermine the role of the respective NSAs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about the sports industry.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: SportSG Vision 2030 seeks to inspire Singaporeans to live better through sports and as part of the eco-system there is indeed the industry's contribution to economy, as a culture of sports in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, there are various platforms and initiatives including ActiveSG as the national movement of sports to engage our people and rally the nation, facilitate the master plan.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But you must also take note that the sports industry is also an evolving landscape.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: That is also in response to the interest among young people, interest among the corporates, local and international businesses.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we will continue to monitor the emerging trends in sports.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, for example, sports development in Asia, its growing interest with China's growth as a global sports power, in the manufacture of sporting goods and the foray of Chinese companies into sports enterprises.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we are looking into such opportunities for Singapore arising from these trends into developing an eco-system that can support sports business development and how we can further leverage on SportSG infrastructure and assets to nurture a market place for ideas and innovations with stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: At Sports Hub, there is a commercial contract that we have with SHPL.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, as mentioned, there are deliverables, there are penalties that are part of the contract.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, they have been taken to task over areas where they have not met the KPIs and we are in continuous discussion with them, monitoring their performance and having their assurance that they are committed to building a sports hub, as what we envisaged.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is our national sports icon and we hope that Singaporeans would also participate in activities at the Sports Hub to help build a strong sporting culture for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: ActiveSG's role is to promote the sporting culture.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Member asked about the academies in football and tennis.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: These are academies' initiatives and programmes that SportSG initiated to bring sports to more people but working closely with the respective National Sports Associations.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I do not think it is a fair statement to say that when you have renowned or very established coaches involved in the academy, it means that it is just elite sports and, therefore, it is at the expense of high performance sports training and development.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I do not think mass or public sports should be denied good coaches, people who have the ability to bring the sports to a higher level and also to cultivate interest among especially young people.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Can I ask the Minister what are our chances of getting this as well as what can we do now, as Singapore together, to increase our chances?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: They are hoping that they can use their credit there.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I am very happy to hear that those above 65 now will have free admission to the gyms as well as the swimming pool.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Because exercising early, from the doctor's point of view, is important for health.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The question on hawker culture, the process now is in the hands of UNESCO.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To be very frank, they will go through their internal assessment.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There is nothing we can do as a country to influence or affect the process.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But I think there is a lot that Singaporeans can do to continue to support hawkers and hawker culture in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many of them deserve our support, whether it is by patronising them or showcasing them or just giving them the kind of exposure that they so deserve.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When there is good food, I am sure we will tell each other about it.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, continue to support and give them good business.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think we are also trying to, in a way, make our hawker centres a lot cleaner, particularly in this period of time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That is also an important part of hawker culture – it is not just the food but also the place.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: How do we have a new standard of public eating spaces in our hawker centres?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it is also something that Singaporeans should think about.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In general, I think we are looking at ways to encourage Singaporeans to adopt an active lifestyle.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When they are young, we are doing as much as we can in the schools, starting this time round, as you can see, our efforts will go into the pre-school sector, getting the teachers involved, getting the programme instituted at the pre-school level, and also getting the parents at the pre-schools involved as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it is really to try to work along the wide range of ages to access sport opportunities, with customised and appropriate measures for each age range.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The first one on the Orchard Youth Belt which I believe Senior Minister of State Sim Ann said that Senior Parliamentary Secretary would mention.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I am not so sure I caught that part of the answer.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Will there be delays because of the current economic situation and what are the broad plans forward?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: In relation to sports, again to the Senior Parliamentary Secretary, yesterday there was quite a stark commentary on the state of sports in The New Paper, written by Leonard Thomas.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I also heard the Senior Parliamentary Secretary say earlier that Ministry and the SportSG does not interfere in the running of the NSAs.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Leonard also mentioned in his article that, and I quote, "I can't help but feel some undercurrent of distrust between NSAs and SportSG." So, I would like to ask what is the type of oversight that SportSG has over the NSAs, especially over drafting of their constitutions, rules and regulations on elections and renewal of their management committees.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We were planning to announce it a few weeks ago.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But because of the COVID-19 situation, we thought that it may not be a good thing to have that kind of announcement.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we are planning for some time later this month.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Following that, we will also be doing some pilots for the type of programming, activities that would rejuvenate the Somerset Belt; programmes that are relevant and interesting for young people throughout the year.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, it is an evolving plan and we look forward to more youth engagement and participation to help us further develop and realise the master plan.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Mr Yam also asked about how we could increase the interest of the public in competitive sport events, especially with the attendance numbers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I think that is where we would first like to develop a strong sporting and interest in sports, as a whole, as a nation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For specific events, we will then have to work closely with the event organiser or the respective NSAs on how to make their sports spectator experience a meaningful and interesting one.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: SportSG has worked at the national-level events, to institute a certain format of the venue atmosphere in terms of how athletes are introduced as they enter the courts or the match venue, in terms of the results announcement, and medal presentation – these have all helped to make it look more professional and also sustain the interest among public.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We also work with the schools because a lot of the students do enjoy the sporting competitions at the school level.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we hope that we will continue to be able to work on this to make it such that going to sports, cheering for athletes would become a way of life for many of our Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As to the relationship between Sport SG and NSAs in areas where Sport SG provides funding for the NSAs to roll out their respective programmes, I think that is where we have the biggest interest because we are using public money, taxpayers' money for sport NSAs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Therefore, things like governance where it is not reflected in the constitution or where there is a lack of rules and regulations or by-laws that does not assure the Government of a structure to make ensure proper accountability, that is where Sports SG will take a keen interest and even direct certain changes in the NSAs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As to the other programmes, we would leave it to the NSAs to set the targets, to roll out the programmes as long as it is beneficial for the sports scene.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In areas where public money is concerned, we would definitely take a much closer look.
